Yes. The latest analysis detected **13.5 hectares of tree-cover loss in 2025**, about 3.9% of the property. The JRC 2020 forest reference classified 98% of the loss area as forest in 2020.

The event has not yet met the tool’s full corroboration rule because no later year was available in the series. Tree-cover loss does not by itself establish the cause or whether the land was permanently deforested.
